claims.text: In CrFeCoNiX alloys, selective oxidation of X controls the formation and persistence of a protective oxide above 900 °C.
Si, Mn, or Al preferentially oxidizes at high temperature in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
The resulting oxide scale is enriched in the oxidized X element.
The X-enriched oxide is compositionally compatible with the CrFeCoNiX substrate.
The X-enriched oxide has a crystallographic structure closely matched to that of the underlying alloy.
The X-enriched oxide has a thermal expansion coefficient closely matched to that of the underlying alloy.
Structural and thermal-expansion compatibility minimizes internal stress in the oxide scale.
Selective oxidation of X limits further oxygen ingress and slows oxide growth.
Reduced stress accumulation suppresses cracking and spallation of the oxide scale.
The protective scale forms a well-adhered, low-stress interlayer at the metal/oxide interface.
The resulting oxide remains coherent, slow-growing, and resistant to thermal stresses during prolonged exposure above 900 °C.
The persistent oxide maintains a low defect density.
CrFeCoNi controls or variants with insufficient X form rapidly growing or crack- and spallation-prone scales under comparable exposure.
Changing X among Si, Mn, and Al should produce measurable differences in oxide coherence, growth rate, adhesion, residual stress, and spallation relative to an X-free control.
The proposed behavior applies to both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys.
The proposed protection may not apply at substantially lower temperatures or under non-oxidizing conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis, intervention, and boundary specify temperatures strictly above 900 °C, whereas the conditions include 900 °C through the notation ≥900 °C.
